source.title: Heat source
source.description: An entity that counts heat, or the energy that becomes heat. Its increase is split between the consumers. A gas source of the Energy dashboard is preselected.

data_description.entity_id: A meter reading that only increases, e.g. in kWh, m³ or L.
data_description.quantity: Heat: already converted, e.g. a heat meter or the heat output a heat pump reports. Energy input: gas, oil or electricity before the boiler or heat pump turns it into heat; the factor follows in the next step.

factor.title: Conversion to heat
factor.description:
How many kWh of heat does 1 {unit} of {name} give?

- Gas in m³: calorific value × z-number × boiler efficiency, about 9 to 10. Calorific value and z-number are on the gas bill.
- Heating oil in L: about 9 (10 kWh/L × boiler efficiency).
- Gas, oil or pellets in kWh: the boiler efficiency, about 0.85 to 0.95.
- Burner run time in h: the heat output of the burner in kW, for a burner without modulation.
- Electricity of an immersion heater: 1.
- Electricity of a heat pump: its seasonal COP, about 3 to 4. More accurate: the heat the heat pump reports itself, as a source that counts heat.

data_description.factor: kWh of heat per unit of the reading.

circuit.description: Radiators behind one pump. Without a running pump, none of them gets heat.

radiator.title: Radiator
radiator.description: Gets a share of the heat by its size and demand.

data_description.name: For example the room.
data_description.circuit: Without a circuit, the radiator is always supplied.
data_description.demand_entity_id: Thermostat, heating demand or valve position in %, or an on/off actuator. Without one, the radiator counts as always heating.

data_description.size_type: By default, all radiators count as equal.
